== EXTRACTION RULES (GEMINI_HANDOFF_BRIEF §3 Task C & §5.2; CODEBOOK.md §§1-9; RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1) ==
1. ACCESSIBILITY GATE:
   - If `Retrieval status` is `not_accessible` (or the paper text below says `[FULL TEXT NOT ACCESSIBLE]`), you MUST set `paper_read = "not accessible"`, set `value = "cannot_tell"`, `where_found = "not accessible"`, and `comment = "full text not accessible"` for ALL 9 fields, and `evidence_quotes = []`. NEVER copy publication year or country from the citation header when the full paper was not read!
2. IF FULL TEXT IS READABLE:
   - Extract each of the 9 fields strictly from the paper text. Write a field value ONLY if the paper explicitly states it; if not stated in the paper, write `"not reported"` in `value` and explain in `comment`. Never guess or infer from context.
   - `publication_year`: 4-digit year printed on the paper/report itself (e.g. `"2024"`), or `"not reported"` if undated. Give exact page/header in `where_found`.
   - `country`: Country or countries studied as stated in the paper (use semicolon-separated names if multiple specific countries, or exact global/regional scope as stated, e.g. `"Global (48 countries)"`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `sample_size`: Exact sample size(s) AND explicit unit(s) of analysis stated in the paper (e.g. `"593 households across 4 neighbourhoods"`, `"128 municipalities; 2,048 observations (2010-2025)"`, `"32 semi-structured interviews"`), or `"not reported"` if pure doctrinal/legal analysis with no empirical sample.
   - `study_design`: Study design as the authors describe it and as operationalized in the methods section (be specific about quantitative/qualitative/quasi-experimental/experimental/review structure).
   - `effect_estimate`: Headline result of the study regarding how the legal, administrative, regulatory, institutional, tenure, tariff/subsidy, or participation factor relates to water/sanitation access/outcomes, with exact printed numbers (point estimates, units, 95% CIs, p-values, sample N) if quantitative, or concise factual headline finding if qualitative (noting `"Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported"` when purely qualitative), in your own words from the paper alone.
   - `risk_of_bias_tool`: Pick the single design-matched tool per `RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1:
     * `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"` (individually randomized trial)
     * `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"` (cluster-randomized trial — check unit of randomization carefully!)
     * `"ROBINS-I"` (non-randomized intervention / quasi-experimental study with a genuine comparator: DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, policy panel FE)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"` (quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without quasi-experimental intervention comparator)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"` (observational longitudinal cohort study without intervention framing)
     * `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"` (primary qualitative study: interviews, focus groups, ethnography, qualitative case study)
     * `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"` (genuine mixed-methods study combining both qualitative and quantitative primary components)
     * `"AMSTAR 2"` (systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with systematic search/screening; NEVER use for non-systematic narrative literature reviews)
     * `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"` (legal-empirical, doctrinal-empirical, jurimetric, or institutional-historical study that fits none of the six conventional designs above)
     * `"NONE"` (fits none of the listed tools, e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model, or non-systematic narrative review/essay without primary empirical data or systematic search — explain why in `comment`)
   - `mechanism_certainty`: Single integer `"0"`, `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, or `"4"` strictly obeying `CODEBOOK.md` §9 and its design ceiling:
     * `"4"` ONLY for randomized trials (`RoB 2`)
     * `"3"` ONLY for `RoB 2` trials OR `ROBINS-I` studies with credible Low/Moderate overall risk of bias
     * All other designs (cross-sectional/JBI, cohort, qualitative/CASP, mixed-methods/MMAT, systematic review/AMSTAR 2, Legal Framework, NONE, or Serious/Critical ROBINS-I) CANNOT exceed `"2"`! (`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).
   - `outcome_flags`: Comma-separated list using ONLY exact `CODEBOOK.md` §5 codes actually studied in the paper (`formal_connection`, `water_access`, `sanitation_access`, `service_coverage`, `service_reliability`, `service_quantity`, `service_quality`, `affordability`, `service_continuity`, `application_success`, `refusal`, `delay`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `mechanism_flags`: Comma-separated list of applicable top-level family codes (`ELIGIBILITY`, `BURDEN`, `DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION`, `ENFORCEMENT`) followed by exact detailed `CODEBOOK.md` §4 codes actually studied in the paper (`documentation`, `tenure`, `property`, `planning`, `zoning`, `building_permit`, `service_area`, `fees`, `procedural_steps`, `delay`, `discretion`, `hardship_exception`, `accommodation`, `administrative_review`, `complaint`, `judicial_review`, `disconnection`, `reconnection`, `sanction`, `participation`, `institutional_fragmentation`, `political_coordination`, `bureaucratic_assistance`), or `"not reported"`.
3. `where_found` AND `evidence_quotes`:

evidence_quotes.quote: Regarding the research design, primary data was derived from the mixed research method of quantitative and qualitative research.
Due to participant hesitancy, the research project achieved only 47% participation from the expected 66 households, resulting in 31 households actually participating in the survey.

(1). Facilitate physical infrastructure upgrading, which included the provision of potable water, electricity, drainage, and sewage infrastructure. (2). Facilitate security of tenure for eligible squatters who occupied state lands prior to 1998 (GovTT, 1998).

All (n = 31) households indicated that they possessed access to an improved supply of water and that the cost of accessing an improved water supply does not exceed 10% of household income. Water supply was direct on-lot/into-dwelling water delivery with 30 households. Merely one household stated that they utilized a public tap as their improved source of water.
Regarding the access to improved sanitation, the majority of households (n = 30) secured the service through the upgrading.

However, the assessment alone does not clarify the factors and measures that contribute to this development. Although the study did not investigate these single factors, the area is located close to major highways, and it was formally connected.

country.comment: Single-case empirical study of Bamboo Settlement #3 in the Tunapuna/Piarco region of Trinidad and Tobago, contextualized within Caribbean Small Island Developing States (CSIDS).
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section 1; PDF p. 3, Figure 1

effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive quantitative metrics and qualitative thematic counts are reported without p-values or confidence intervals (despite mentioning a one-sample t-test in Section 4). Note minor internal arithmetic inconsistency in the paper on tenure security: Section 5 (p. 7) sums 14 formal title + 2 COC + 10 HDC agreements = 26 (out of 31, leaving 5 without tenure security) as '25 households possessing tenure security, with a relatively small number, 5 households having no clear tenure security', while Section 6 (p. 8) states '26 possessed access to the dimensions of Secure Tenure' alongside a typo '25 households that possessed no clear form of tenure security'.
effect_estimate.value: In Bamboo Settlement #3 (a Designated Area under the Squatter Regularization Program and State Land [Regularization of Tenure] Act 1998), 31/31 surveyed households (100%) had improved water access costing <10% of household income: 30/31 had direct on-lot/into-dwelling water delivery (mean quarterly water cost $219.99, or 1.034% of St. George County mean quarterly income of $21,271.00) and 1/31 used a public standpipe ($33.75 quarterly, or 0.1586% of income). For sanitation, 30/31 households had improved sanitation (27/31 via septic tank/pit and 3/31 [10%] via sewer-connected flush/pour toilets), while 1/31 lacked improved sanitation due to high financial repair/maintenance costs (and 2/31 required major septic system repairs). For tenure security, 14/31 held formal title, 2/31 held a Certificate of Comfort, 10/31 had Housing Development Corporation titling/engagement arrangements (n = 15 thematic subset), and 5/31 lacked clear tenure security (reported as 25/31 with secure tenure in Section 5 and 26 in Section 6). Overall, 25/31 households met 4 of 5 UN upgrading dimensions and 6/31 met 3 of 5 (0/31 met hazard-free location due to floodplain siting); no confidence intervals or p-values are reported.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 5-7, Section 5, Table 2, and Table 4; PDF pp. 7-8, Section 6

mechanism_certainty.comment: Design ceiling is 2 (mixed-methods single-case study appraised with MMAT). Rated 1 because the study empirically documents post-upgrading water, sanitation, and tenure outcomes within a Designated Area under the Squatter Regularization Program, but does not cross-tabulate tenure status against WASH access or directly observe the administrative mechanism linking legal regularization rules to water/sanitation connection; the authors explicitly state (PDF p. 8, Section 6) that the assessment alone does not clarify the specific factors and measures contributing to the observed outcomes.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 4, Section 3; PDF pp. 5-7, Section 5 and Table 4; PDF p. 8, Section 6

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines squatter regularization and pre-1998/pre-2000 eligibility cutoffs under the State Land (Regularization of Tenure) Act 1998, Certificates of Comfort, formal title deeds, and proof of dwelling ownership for grants (ELIGIBILITY: tenure, property, documentation); registration of Bamboo Settlement #3 as a 'Designated Area' eligible for infrastructure upgrading funds (service_area); outdated planning laws, illegal agricultural-to-residential land-use change, and non-enforcement of zoning (planning, zoning); water tariffs, sanitation repair costs, insufficient home improvement subsidies, and titling/taxation costs (BURDEN: fees); and slow upgrading pace and lack of formal HDC engagement to initiate regularization (delay).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, tenure, property, documentation, service_area, planning, zoning, fees, delay
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section 1; PDF p. 4, Section 3; PDF pp. 6-7, Section 5, Table 1, Table 2, and Table 4; PDF pp. 7-8, Section 6

outcome_flags.comment: Primary survey measures household access to improved water (water_access), direct on-lot/into-dwelling piped delivery vs. standpipe and sewer vs. septic connections (formal_connection), access to improved sanitation (sanitation_access), and water expenditure as a share of income plus financial barriers to sanitation maintenance (affordability). Note that Table 1 defines the improved water indicator as including >=20 liters/person/day within <=1 hour collection time, though separate volumetric quantity metrics are not reported in Section 5.
